title: The Age of the Agent: Flo Crivello
talk_summary: Flo Crivello (Lindy) argues that agents will remove business friction the way YouTube removed media gatekeepers, and demos a 'society of Lindies' where specialized agents (tool-creation, API-spec research, manager, engineers, auth specialist, QA) collaborate to build integrations. The talk is mostly vision and product demo; the only concrete mechanism is a hierarchical multi-agent build pipeline with a QA loop back to engineers before PR submission.

takeaways.technique: Specialized role pipeline with QA bounce-back
takeaways.what_they_do: A top-level 'tool creation' agent delegates to a research agent (finds OpenAPI spec + docs), a manager agent that splits work across engineer agents (including a dedicated auth-code engineer), then a QA agent that sends failures back to the engineer and only submits a PR on pass.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they pass the work to QA engineering Lindy that does the work and if it doesn't work sends it back to the software engineer if it works submit a PR
takeaways.numbers: speaker says the system is '70 or 80% of the way there'

takeaways.technique: Manager agent decomposes a single instruction into parallel engineer tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: A manager agent takes one high-level instruction and splits it across many engineer agents working the same task, rather than one agent doing the whole integration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: talks to this Lindy that's a manager Lind just splits up the task across many Engineers

takeaways.technique: Research agent fetches OpenAPI spec and docs before coding
takeaways.what_they_do: Before engineers write an integration, a dedicated agent goes online to retrieve the OpenAPI spec and web documentation, so downstream agents code against a real contract instead of guessing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: goes online and finds the open API spec and the online web documentation
